title: fix(app-shell): Studio's Default value control for rating, slider and progress is the number control (objectui#11966)
body:
Fixes #11966

Clause-②: no

Studio's field inspector gave `rating`, `slider` and `progress` fields the text *Default value* control. These types store a number, so `FieldSchema` refused the string the control wrote (`defaultValue: '3'`, "expected number, received string"). They now get the existing number control, and the default saves as a number.

## What changed

- `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`, `defaultValueKind`: the number editor now serves every type in the spec's numeric value class, `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, instead of a hand list of `number`, `currency` and `percent`. The hand list is what left these three types out. The computed `summary`, also in that class, still gets no editor (`isComputed`), and the no-default list is untouched. Reading the spec's set follows `takesPicklist` in the same file and `ObjectApiPanel.tsx`, which already read the spec's sets.
- New pin `ObjectFieldInspector.numericDefault-11966.test.tsx`, through the real inspector in a host that applies each patch as the designers do.
- `.changeset/11966-numeric-default.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

No other file is touched. No export, prop, type member or language-pack key is added.

## Measurements against the dispatch hypotheses

**H1, the number control writes a number: confirmed.** Each type is mounted with the bounds objectstack's showcase field zoo declares (`f_rating` max 5; `f_slider` min 0, max 100, step 5; `f_progress` min 0, max 100). Typing writes a JS number (3, 3, 40), and `FieldSchema` parses the field. Emptying the box removes the default. Controls: `text` keeps the text control and writes the string `'3'`. `number` keeps the number control. `summary` still renders none.

**H2, bounds: the range half is not done, and this PR does not claim it.**
- What the spec declares, read in `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 `data/field.zod.ts`: these types can declare the generic numeric `min` and `max`, which the runtime record validator enforces on writes of `rating`, `slider` and `progress`. `step` is the slider's UI increment and explicitly not a stored-value constraint. `scale` and `precision` apply to `rating` and `slider`. The spec has no `progress`-specific 0–100 bound.
- The spec does not refuse an out-of-range default at parse. `FieldSchema` admits a `rating` with max 5 and default 7, a `slider` (0–100) with default 140, and a `progress` (0–100) with default -5. The literal default is judged only against the stored value contract, a finite number. So the condition "the control must not write it" does not trigger. A test pins this reading: if the spec ever refuses one, it goes red.
- The existing number editor, `InspectorNumberField` in `inspectors/_shared.tsx`, takes no range. Its props are `label`, `value`, `onCommit`, `placeholder`, `disabled` and `required`. Giving it `min` and `max` means a new prop in a file outside this claim's surface, so it is not done here (route under Acceptance notes). Guarding the commit inside this file does not work either. The control commits on every keystroke, so a lower bound would refuse the first digit of a valid value: with min 10, typing 15 starts at 1.

**H3, a stored string default: not converted, but not shown.**
- A `rating` field stored with `defaultValue: '3'` keeps the string `'3'` when Required is ticked.
- Typing a number over it replaces it.
- ⚠️ It is not shown. The number box reads its value only when it is a number, so the stored string appears as an empty box. A `number`, `currency` or `percent` field with a string default already behaves this way.
- Showing it would need one of three things: a display that disagrees with storage (the box reads 3 while `'3'` is stored), a placeholder (which would change the `number` kind for all six types), or new copy (outside the surface).
- The pin asserts the box shows no number, so the box never claims a number the field does not carry.

**H4: `ObjectFieldInspector.recordNoDefault-11947.test.tsx` stays green** in the run below.

## Ablation

The fix line was swapped back to the hand list with `ablation-replace.mjs` from the objectstack checkout: anchor 1 → 0, blob `aa8e6b918694` → `2d29ccc40354`. Then the new pin ran: `Tests  5 failed | 8 passed (13)`.

The 5 failures are the expected ones: the three per-type writes and two of the stored-string cases. Under the text control, the stored string shows and a typed number saves as a string. These stay green, as expected: the controls, the cases that read the spec, and the unrelated edit.

The restore is proven: the blob equals HEAD (`aa8e6b918694`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates (HEAD `41407870a`)

- **Closure build, type-check and tests: one run under the container's verify lock.** It printed `41407870a`, `BUILD-CLOSURE-OK`, `TYPECHECK-OK` and `TESTS-OK`, then `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
  - The build was `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/app-shell^..."`: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exited 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin.
  - vitest ran the 20 test files that import `ObjectFieldInspector`, the new pin, and `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`: `Test Files  22 passed (22)` and `Tests  336 passed (336)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, "✅  2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0, "✅  No changeset declares a `major` bump."
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only".
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0, "✅  check-control-bytes: OK".
- Derived by hand from this repo's `check:*` scripts for a new mocked test, a spec import and a changeset. Each exited 0: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check:designer-field-key-parity`.
- **eslint on the two touched `.ts` / `.tsx` files:** exit 0, with 0 errors and 11 warnings. The warnings are all `no-explicit-any`, on lines this diff does not touch. The same file at the base also reads 0 errors and 11 warnings.
  - The narrowing is a measurement, not a skipped run. The config's population is `**/*.{ts,tsx}`, and `--format json` counted 2 files.
  - The config sets no `parserOptions.project`: `--print-config` shows empty parser options. So linting is not type-aware, and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- NOT MEASURED: the eager-closure budget is read by CI's budget bot.

## Acceptance notes

- **Route for the range half (not taken, outside the surface):** `InspectorNumberField` could take optional `min` and `max` (and `step`) and forward them to its `Input`. It is not exported from the package entry. A native number input's bounds only steer the spinner; they do not stop typing. A stricter range would first need the spec to refuse an out-of-range default.
- **Observation, not filed: an out-of-range default parses but would likely be refused at insert.** This was read from objectstack source at `51290bca` and not measured end to end. `FieldSchema` does not judge a default against `min` / `max`. The engine applies defaults before `validateRecord`, which enforces `min` / `max` on these types. So a `rating` with max 5 and default 7 would likely be refused (`max_value`) on every insert that omits the field. No producer of such a default is named.
- **Observation, not filed: the numeric section is also a hand list.** The inspector's numeric section (`isNumeric`: precision, scale, min, max) lists only `number`, `currency` and `percent`. So Studio offers no `min` or `max` for `rating`, `slider` or `progress`, while the showcase's producers declare them in code. This is not a refused write.
- Docs: no guide page describes the inspector's default-value control per type, so there is nothing to update.
